Before running pytest, set HLM_TEST_DSN to a disposable database. If the tests load the local embedder, set ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 in the new terminal.

In zsh, `*.md` is expanded before grep runs and may fail with `no matches found`. Quote the pattern: `grep -rn sweeper docs --include='*.md'`.
Do not bypass the pre-commit hook. Add a narrow scanner allowlist entry for the fake-token fixture path, then commit with verification enabled.
Do not select a DF threshold using the sealed corpus. Tune on dev only, then score the sealed set once in aggregate for final confirmation.

Do not run the migration against the shared dev database; use W2b’s own hlm_test_<ws> database. Plain `alembic upgrade head` is ambiguous because migration history has a second branch head—target the labelled main-branch head.

`ssh` may consume the loop's stdin, so only the first host is processed; use `ssh -n`. Also, `pkill -f hlmemo.worker` may match and kill its own SSH session; use an anchored pattern, pidfile, or service manager.
Keep word_similarity_threshold at 0.9: lowering it caused GIN rechecks to touch every chunk, making single-term queries take 3–7 s with no recall gain.
The /mcp SSE stream must pass through unbuffered. Reading its full response body would prevent headers and pings from flushing and leave clients hanging.

Run the ~10-minute deploy detached on the host and poll its status; do not rely on the laptop’s SSH session staying open. On a first deploy, wait for TLS certificate issuance before treating a public /ready timeout as failure and rolling back.
Take and verify the backup before stopping api and worker; a failed backup must not leave production down. Apply migrations to the labelled main-branch head, not plain `alembic upgrade head`.

Do not ALTER embeddings.vec or rebuild a single HNSW index for a model switch. Vectors are stored untyped with per-row dims and model@revision; switching models requires a re-embed job and a per-model partial ANN index.
Set ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 for the new CLI and CI runs: ONNX Runtime's telemetry thread can abort the process at shutdown (exit 134).
Do not apply firewall rules account-wide: the account hosts other production machines. Target the HLMemo VM explicitly.
A 40 MB memory.write must use keyset-paged chunk reads and token-capped embedding batches; loading all chunks at once previously OOM-killed the worker.

parsed.summary: Orbitq manages job retries using an exponential backoff strategy starting at 2 seconds, with a 20% jitter applied to each delay. The backoff duration doubles per attempt, capped at 5 minutes. By default, jobs are allowed 5 attempts before being moved to the jobs_dead table, though this can be overridden per job using the @job(max_attempts=...) decorator. Dead-lettered jobs trigger alerts in the queue-alerts channel and are purged from the database after 30 days. The retry count is tracked in the attempts column of the jobs table. Specific job types, such as payment webhooks, are excluded from retries. Dead jobs can be manually replayed using the orbitq replay command, which resets the attempt counter.

Uploaded attachments are excluded from these dumps and are instead synced to offsite storage using rclone. While current backups are unencrypted, there are plans to encrypt offsite copies using age. parsed.summary: The Kestrel API implements rate limiting using a token-bucket middleware applied to all /v1 routes. The standard limit is 120 requests per minute per API key, controlled by the RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN configuration. Bursts up to 2x the limit are permitted for 10 seconds. Rate limiting is enforced per API key rather than per client address. When limits are exceeded, the system returns an HTTP 429 status code with a Retry-After header, and the event is tracked via the ratelimit_rejected_total metric. Internal service keys and the /health endpoint are exempt from these limits. The rate-limiting buckets are stored in Redis with a two-minute TTL.

The system defaults to UTC for cron_timezone, which is the current configuration for production after a migration from Europe/Berlin to avoid daylight-saving issues. The nightly settlement job is scheduled for 22:30 UTC, and the report job runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC. If a worker is down, missed fires are executed once upon startup rather than replayed individually. Orbitq exposes the next_fire_at timestamp as a metric for monitoring.
